description: Cuts and keeps the segment of a sound between start and end. Pinned to submode 1 (times in seconds); submodes 2 (sample counts) and 3 (grouped-sample counts) can be curated separately. Duration model 'end - start' is sample-exact: the splice windows fade the block's edges in place and do NOT lengthen it, and with splice 0 the output is a verbatim sample-exact copy of input[start:end]. Works on mono and stereo input.
musical_use: The basic surgical edit: save a favoured portion of a soundfile, or isolate a short, timbrally evolving section to time-stretch (then cut part of the result and stretch again). Classic workflows: pre-process key portions of two sounds before a morph and reinsert them; collect segments from several files toward a collage; and - mid-chain - trim a long output from an extend/granulation process down to the region you actually want before further (and now faster) processing. A long splice gives a smooth cutoff, a short one an abrupt cutoff, and a zero splice usually clicks; for removing silence or interior material use sfedit excise instead.

start.description: Time in the input where the kept segment begins (runtime-enforced 0 to the input duration: 2.5 on a 2 s file is refused with 'Value (2.500000) out of range (0.000000 to 2.000000)'). If start > end the binary silently swaps them (verified byte-identical output) rather than erroring. Scalar only.

end.description: Time in the input where the kept segment ends (runtime-enforced 0 to the input duration; values past the file end are refused, not clamped). Output duration is exactly end - start. Scalar only.

splice.description: Splice window in milliseconds applied inside both ends of the kept block (CDP's internal default is 15; enforced range 0-5000). Does not change the output duration. Must fit twice within the block: 600 ms on a 1 s cut aborts with 'Edited portion is too short for specified splicelen.'. 0 gives a verbatim cut (verified sample-exact) that may click. Scalar only - a breakpoint file is refused.

examples.description: Keep the middle second of a sound with default 15 ms splices.
examples.expected_use: Exactly 1.0 s output; edges faded over 15 ms inside the block, interior untouched.

examples.description: Verbatim splice-less extraction for sample-exact downstream work.
examples.expected_use: Bit-faithful copy of the selected samples (may click if the cut points are not at zero crossings).

known_issues: start > end is silently accepted and swapped (verified: '1.5 0.5' produces a byte-identical file to '0.5 1.5') - callers relying on CDP to catch reversed arguments will not get an error.
start/end are runtime-range-checked against the input duration; an end past the file's length is refused ('out of range (0.000000 to 2.000000)' on a 2 s file), not clamped.
The splice window must fit twice inside the kept block, or CDP aborts with 'ERROR: Edited portion is too short for specified splicelen.' (runtime- and parameter-dependent).
All three parameters reject breakpoint files ('ERROR: Cannot read parameter N [...]: brkpnt_files not permitted.', N = 1-3).
